jobs.description:
**Center for Latino Adolescent and Family Health at Johns Hopkins School of Nursing**

**Title of Position:** LPN Clinical Research Coordinator

The Center for Latino Adolescent and Family Health’s (CLAFH’s) mission is to eliminate health inequities and promote overall wellbeing among Latino adolescents and their families. While our work is Latino-focused, our research and resources are applicable to initiatives aimed at ending inequities for other groups. CLAFH’s core work focuses on developing, evaluating, and disseminating family-based interventions and nurse-driven models of health care delivery designed to mitigate harmful social determinants of health, eliminate health inequities, increase Latino engagement in health care, and promote life opportunities. For more information about our center, please see our website.

**Description of Duties and Responsibilities**

The **LPN** Clinical Research Coordinator will oversee the day-to-day implementation of CLAFH's community-based behavioral health and prevention programs, with a focus on coordinating field operations, supervising research and program staff, and supporting the delivery of nurse-led and family-centered services. The position will involve direct engagement with adolescents, young adults, and families, primarily in the South Bronx.

The LPN Clinical Research Coordinator will:

* Oversee daily field operations and implementation of community-based health and prevention programs, including home visits, community outreach, screening, prevention education, and referral and linkage to services.
* Coordinate and supervise field-based research and program staff, including community health workers, family coaches, and other personnel involved in program implementation.
* Develop and coordinate staff schedules, field assignments, training activities, and ongoing supervision to ensure timely and effective program delivery.
* Perform clinical duties within the scope of LPN licensure, including health screenings, patient education, documentation, and other nursing services under appropriate clinical supervision.
* Oversee participant recruitment, enrollment, retention, follow-up, and fidelity to evidence-based and community-derived intervention protocols.
* Support nurse-led care coordination, including identifying participant health and social needs, facilitating referrals, and following up with families to support engagement in appropriate services.
* Coordinate with community partners, health care providers, and social service organizations to support program implementation and strengthen referral and linkage processes.
* Monitor program activities, service delivery, and staff performance to ensure adherence to project protocols, quality standards, and funder requirements.
* Work collaboratively with project leadership and evaluation staff to ensure accurate and timely collection, documentation, and reporting of participant and program data.
* Assist with continuous quality improvement activities, identifying implementation challenges and opportunities to strengthen program reach, engagement, and service delivery.
* Ensure adherence to relevant confidentiality, participant protection, ethical, and regulatory requirements, including HIPAA and applicable human subjects research protocols.
* Support preparation for project meetings, staff trainings, site visits, and other program-related activities.
* Perform other duties as assigned in support of CLAFH's community-based research and intervention programs.

**Qualifications for the Position**

* Current, unrestricted Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN) license in New York State required.
* Graduate of an accredited practical nursing program required.
* Experience in community health, public health, adolescent health, behavioral health, or related service delivery settings preferred.
* Experience coordinating or supervising community-based research or program staff preferred.
* Experience implementing evidence-based interventions, conducting health screenings, and supporting care coordination preferred.
* Familiarity with substance use prevention, mental health services, and health and social service systems preferred.
* Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish preferred.
* Bronx residency and familiarity with South Bronx communities preferred.
* Experience working with Latino, Black, and other historically underserved communities preferred.
* Strong organizational, interpersonal, supervisory, and communication skills.
* Ability to manage multiple program activities and coordinate staff in a fast-paced, deadline-focused environment.
* Willingness and ability to work in community-based settings, including participant homes and partner organizations.
* Flexibility to work occasional evenings or weekends as needed for community outreach and program activities.
* Strong commitment to addressing health inequities and supporting adolescent and family wellbeing.

**Supervisory Relationships:** Reports to the Principal Investigator and designated CLAFH leadership. Provides operational supervision to assigned field-based research and program staff. Clinical duties are performed under the supervision required by applicable New York State nursing regulations.

Pay: $60,000.00 - $70,000.00 per year

Work Location: In person

jobs.title: Strategic Account Manager
jobs.description:
**About The Role**
------------------

Hello Patient is hiring a Strategic Account Manager to own the health, retention, and growth of our customer accounts from signature through post-go-live. You will be the primary relationship holder for your accounts, responsible for ensuring customers consistently realize value from Mia, identifying risks early, and helping customers expand how they use HelloPatient over time.

This is a proactive, ownership-driven role. You’ll maintain a clear, up-to-date understanding of how each account is performing, monitor key signals to catch issues before they escalate, and partner closely with internal teams to drive resolution.

Customers should view you as a trusted partner, essentially an extension of their team who understands their business, not just a point of contact for a software vendor.

While you’ll stay involved during the initial implementation to establish the relationship and ensure smooth handoffs and communication, your core responsibility ramps up after go-live to own the customer experience, manage communication and expectations, and be accountable for long-term customer success.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

### **Own Account Health**

* Track how the agents are performing across your accounts, including containment, transfers, and reschedule, cancel and confirm rates. Dig into anything unusual before the customer notices it.
* Review call logs and transfers to find where the agent falls short, and suggest fixes to the call flow.
* Turn issues into clear tickets for Product and Engineering, follow them through to resolution, and keep customers updated along the way.

### **Manage Customer Relationships**

* Be the day-to-day point of contact for your accounts. Build a trusted advisor relationship so customers see you as part of their team, not just a vendor contact.
* Run regular check-ins and program reviews, and send a clear status recap after each one.
* Support customers through soft launch, go-live and ongoing agent updates, like new locations, providers, voice and script changes.
* Work with Product, Engineering, QA, Sales and Solutions to get customers what they need, and wear whatever hat the day calls for.
* Join onsite visits, whiteboarding sessions and industry events.

### **Drive Performance & Growth**

* Build recurring performance reports and use them to help customers understand the value they're getting from Mia.
* Help build ROI models from customer data and turn them into clear stories for customer leadership.
* Spot expansion opportunities, such as new agents, chatbot, billing, referrals and new locations, and help Sales and Solution Engineers scope them.
* Support order forms, renewals and invoicing follow-up.

**What We're Looking For**
--------------------------

### **Must have:**

* 3+ years in account management, customer success or a similar client-facing role.
* Strong written and verbal communication. You can read between the lines, build excitement and handle pushback with confidence.
* A strong storyteller who can turn data into a clear story about value.
* Collaborative and works well with cross-functional teams. You're happy to wear multiple hats.
* Strong attention to detail, so nothing falls through the cracks between customers and internal teams.
* Comfortable with data. You can work in spreadsheets, read dashboards and explain what the numbers mean.
* Proactive and comfortable with ambiguity. You know when to solve a problem yourself and when to escalate.
* You love building from the ground up. You're open to change, can pivot quickly and do well in a fast-paced startup.

### **Preferred:**

* Experience in healthcare, health tech or working with medical practices.
* You use AI or automation tools every day to work faster.
* Background in practice operations, revenue cycle or patient scheduling.
* Some exposure to SQL, BI tools or call center metrics.

**Compensation**
----------------

**Base salary:** $80K–$110K

**Equity:** Meaningful ownership in a fast-growing healthtech startup  
  
**About Hello Patient**

Hello Patient is transforming healthcare communication through advanced conversational AI. Our founding team spent 3.5 years scaling Carbon Health's technology during hypergrowth, where we saw firsthand how much clinical time gets wasted on basic communication—great clinicians buried in admin work, patients stuck in phone tag.

Our AI platform proactively engages patients through perfectly timed calls and texts, resolving complex interactions end-to-end—from scheduling to billing to retention. Built with security and compliance at its core, our technology integrates with existing healthcare infrastructure to deliver 24/7 patient engagement.

Backed by Scale and 8VC, we're building the future of healthcare communication, one conversation at a time.

Compensation Range: $80K - $110K

jobs.description:
**COME JOIN OUR TEAM!**

**OUR TEAM**

Maverick Studios is where creativity meets impact. As the in-house agency for Inspire Brands, we craft award-winning work that spans design, video, photography, print, and beyond. Serving six iconic brands—Arby’s, Buffalo Wild Wings, Baskin-Robbins, Dunkin’, Jimmy John’s, and Sonic—our team is a powerhouse of collaboration and passion. We’re all about delivering best-in-class creativity, innovation, and solutions that resonate across every project.

**OUR CULTURE**

At Inspire Brands, we’re not just dreamers; we’re doers. We thrive on innovation and welcome bold ideas at every level, from the kitchen to the boardroom. Here, taking risks and thinking differently aren’t just encouraged—they’re celebrated. It’s how we started, and it’s how we succeed.

**ABOUT THE ROLE**  
Do you thrive on organization, coordination, and keeping complex projects moving? As a **Traditional Marketing Project Coordinator** at Maverick Studios, you'll play a critical role in supporting the execution of traditional marketing initiatives across multiple Inspire Brands.

From point-of-purchase materials and menu systems to packaging updates, photo shoots, promotional merchandising, and in-store marketing collateral, you'll help ensure projects are accurately built, tracked, routed, and delivered from intake through final production.

You'll partner closely with Project Managers, Account Managers, Creative teams, Proofreading, Brand Marketing partners, and external vendors to support the successful delivery of marketing assets that appear in restaurants across the country.

**WHAT YOU’LL OWN**

* **Traditional Marketing Intake Partner:** Review incoming marketing requests (e.g., POP, packaging, menus, photo shoots, merchandising, print collateral, promotions, etc.) for completeness and accuracy before building in Workfront.
* **Workfront Builder:** Set up traditional marketing projects, align timelines, assign tasks, and track deliverables through completion.
* **Production Coordinator:** Support the execution of packaging, menu, POP, and marketing collateral projects by coordinating assets, approvals, specifications, and production requirements.
* **Feedback Router:** Capture and route feedback from Brand Marketing, Client Relations, Creative, Proofreading, and Production partners to ensure revisions are documented and communicated clearly.
* **Asset Tracker:** Maintain project documentation, version control, routing records, and asset libraries within Workfront, SharePoint, and other team systems.
* **Photo Shoot Support Partner:** Assist with planning and coordination activities for photo shoots, including project setup, timelines, asset collection, deliverables tracking, and post-shoot organization.
* **Delivery Manager:** Upload, distribute, and archive final files to approved repositories and distribution channels.
* **Accuracy Advocate:** Ensure all assets, specifications, and supporting documentation are properly labeled, organized, QA'd, approved, and finalized before release.

**WHAT YOU BRING**

* **Experience:** 1-2 years in a marketing, creative operations, project support, production coordination, or agency role (internship or entry-level experience counts).
* **Tool Readiness:** Familiarity with Workfront, Smartsheets, SharePoint, or similar systems, or a strong eagerness to learn quickly.
* **Production Awareness:** Basic understanding of traditional marketing deliverables such as packaging, menus, POP materials, photo shoots, print production, and marketing collateral.
* **Organized Mindset:** A love of lists, timelines, status updates, and keeping projects neat, tidy, and trackable.
* **Communication Skills:** Clear and proactive communicator who can manage updates across multiple stakeholders and project teams.
* **Detail Obsessed:** You catch the small things (file names, version control, specifications, deadlines, and approvals) that keep projects running smoothly.
* **Collaborative Spirit:** A team-first attitude. You're dependable, approachable, and always willing to lend a hand.

**WHY YOU’LL LOVE IT HERE**

* **People-First Culture:** Join a supportive, collaborative team that values growth and shared wins.
* **Creative Exposure:** Learn the inner workings of a full-service in-house agency and contribute to projects for six iconic brands.
* **Career Growth:** Build foundational project management skills with clear pathways to grow into Project Manager and beyond.
* **Team Spirit:** Expect kudos, brainstorms, and plenty of snacks along the way.
* **Perks & Personality:** Free ice cream, cold brew, and a beer/wine wall fuel the fun.

**EDUCATION QUALIFICATIONS**

* Minimum 4 years – Bachelor’s Degree
* Bachelor’s degree in marketing, business, or related fields and/or experience working in a brand marketing role or agency environment

  
Inspire is a multi-brand restaurant company whose portfolio includes more than 33,000 Arby’s, Baskin-Robbins, Buffalo Wild Wings, Dunkin’, Jimmy John’s, and SONIC restaurants worldwide.  
  
We’re made up of some of the world’s most iconic restaurant brands, but we’re much more than just a restaurant company. We’re a team of hundreds of thousands who individually and collectively are changing the way people eat, drink, and gather around the table. We know that food is much more than a staple—it’s an experience. At Inspire, that’s our purpose: to ignite and nourish flavorful experiences.

**About Us**
------------

  

Georgia Tech prides itself on its technological resources, collaborations, high-quality student body, and its commitment to building an outstanding and diverse community of learning, discovery, and creation. We strongly encourage applicants whose values align with our institutional values, as outlined in our strategic plan. These values include academic excellence, diversity of thought and experience, inquiry and innovation, collaboration and community, and ethical behavior and stewardship. Georgia Tech has policies to promote a healthy work-life balance and is aware that attracting faculty may require meeting the needs of two careers.

**About Georgia Tech**
  
Georgia Tech is a top-ranked public research university situated in the heart of Atlanta, a diverse and vibrant city with numerous economic and cultural strengths. The Institute serves more than 45,000 students through top-ranked undergraduate, graduate, and executive programs in engineering, computing, science, business, design, and liberal arts. Georgia Tech's faculty attracted more than $1.4 billion in research awards this past year in fields ranging from biomedical technology to artificial intelligence, energy, sustainability, semiconductors, neuroscience, and national security. Georgia Tech ranks among the nation's top 20 universities for research and development spending and No. 1 among institutions without a medical school.

**Georgia Tech's Mission and Values**
  
Georgia Tech's mission is to develop leaders who advance technology and improve the human condition. The Institute has nine key values that are foundational to everything we do:

1. Students are our top priority.

2. We strive for excellence.

3. We thrive on diversity.

4. We celebrate collaboration.

5. We champion innovation.

6. We safeguard freedom of inquiry and expression.

7. We nurture the well-being of our community.

8. We act ethically.

9. We are responsible stewards.

Over the next decade, Georgia Tech will become an example of inclusive innovation, a leading technological research university of unmatched scale, relentlessly committed to serving the public good; breaking new ground in addressing the biggest local, national, and global challenges and opportunities of our time; making technology broadly accessible; and developing exceptional, principled leaders from all backgrounds ready to produce novel ideas and create solutions with real human impact.

The School of Civil and Environmental Engineering at Georgia Tech currently has more than 650 undergraduate students, nearly 320 graduate students, 55 tenure-track faculty members, and 4 Professors of the Practice. Twenty-six faculty members hold endowed chairs or professorships with 30% of them being women faculty. The School's Strategic Vision is available at www.ce.gatech.edu/strategic-vision. The Capacity Building Project Coordinator will provide direct support to the GASC Capacity Building Network for Community Safety, assisting in the implementation of technical assistance, training, and resource development for community-based organizations (CBOs). The Project Coordinator will work closely with the Capacity Building Project Manager to ensure smooth program operations, coordinate service delivery, and track program milestones. This role will be instrumental in supporting CBOs in their organizational development and enhancing their ability to deliver effective community violence intervention programs.

**Program Delivery & Strategic Direction**

* Assist in the execution of capacity-building initiatives, ensuring CBOs receive timely and relevant support.
* Coordinate training sessions, workshops, and technical assistance activities with The Network Training Coordinator and Subject Matter Experts (SMEs).
* Serve as a liaison between community partners, technical assistance providers, and program staff.
* Maintain accurate program documentation, including training participation logs and organizational assessments.
* Track Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to measure the success of capacity-building efforts.
* Provide direct support to CBOs, connecting them with appropriate resources and funding opportunities.
* Ensure all grant and contract deliverables are met in collaboration with program leadership.
* Assist in the development of toolkits, guidance materials, and best practice documents for community partners.

jobs.title: Clinical Research Coordinator 2, MOSAAIC Study for Asian Americans
jobs.description:
**Department**

BSD IPP - MOSAAIC

**About the Department**

The Institute for Population and Precision Health (IPPH), located in the Biological Sciences Division, integrates a wide spectrum of factors such as human health behaviors, environmental factors, social and economic factors, policies and genetic determinants of health, into studies focused on the treatment and prevention of disease, as well as the maintenance of wellness. Leveraging and integrating the University of Chicago’s considerable institutional strength in population science with research spanning diverse fields such as genetic medicine, cancer epidemiology, microbiome, and epigenomics, the Institute will have the common goal of improving human health outcomes. Another major goal of the Institute will be to develop a new multidisciplinary training program to equip researchers with emerging tools and methods to conduct precision health research within a population health framework. Our faculty lead research projects in biostatistics, epidemiology and health services research and participate in interdisciplinary teams with faculty in other departments to address complex problems in health and healthcare, in our communities and around the globe.

**Job Summary**

The University of Chicago's Institute for Population and Precision Health (IPPH) is seeking a Clinical Research Coordinator 2 to support its portfolio of federally funded population health research, with a primary focus on the Multi-ethnic Observational Study in American Asian and Pacific Islander Communities (MOSAAIC) — a landmark NHLBI-funded epidemiological cohort study aimed at addressing critical gaps in cardiovascular, metabolic, pulmonary, and mental health research for Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander communities.  
  
The University of Chicago serves as one of five national clinical and community field centers for MOSAAIC, with a goal of enrolling 2,000 Chicago-area participants through community-based outreach, mobile data collection, clinical phenotyping, and biospecimen collection. The study collects data across a broad range of health domains, including heart health, diabetes, lung health, and mental health, as well as social determinants of health such as environmental exposures and access to care. The Clinical Research Coordinator 2 will support the full research lifecycle across this and related IPPH studies — including participant recruitment and retention, IRB compliance, data and specimen collection, quality control, and milestone reporting — working closely with Scientific Directors and the Research Manager to advance research that promotes health equity and reduces disparities in historically underrepresented populations.  
  
This at-will position is wholly or partially funded by contractual grant funding which is renewed under provisions set by the grantor of the contract. Employment will be contingent upon the continued receipt of these grant funds and satisfactory job performance.

**Responsibilities**

* Coordination and quality control management for observational and interventional, including both clinic and community-based studies, within the Institute for Population and Precision Health.
* Support operational execution of multi-institutional and some international studies, many of which are federally funded or funded by pharmaceutical sponsors.
* Oversee the collection of clinical data, survey data, environmental data, and associated samples and biospecimens.
* Manage IRB submissions, amendments, and continuing reviews; develop and refine data collection instruments; enforce implementation accuracy and study staff protocol compliance; and deliver continuous milestone reporting — including progress, successes, and emerging challenges — to study leadership.
* Drive participant engagement through active coordination of subject screening, recruitment, informed consent, data and specimen collection, and longitudinal follow-up and retention strategies.
* Monitor study participants, schedule, and conduct study-related procedures (eg. interviews, phlebotomies, and follow-ups) and establish data quality control checks.
* Work with the Scientific Directors and Research Manager in the planning, development, and evaluation of research.
* Coordination of data acquisition, entry, QC, and query response, ensuring timely and accurate data flow in compliance with study protocols and sponsor or regulatory requirements.
* Assist in the development of new projects and preparation of study reports, and manuscripts for publication.
* Assist in the preparation of presentations, media, and curricular materials relating to research.
* Accountable for all tasks in moderately complex clinical studies.
* Assists with various professional, organizational, and operational tasks under moderate supervision.
* Facilitates and participates in the daily activities of moderately complex clinical studies and performs various activities including patient data retrieval, documenting clinical research records, and participation in program audits.
* Uses knowledge of clinical studies to coordinate the collection of analyzable clinical research data and/or samples with a limited to moderate degree of independence. Contributes to the problem solving on assigned clinical research studies and tasks.
* Performs other related work as needed.

**Minimum Qualifications**

**Education:**

Minimum requirements include a college or university degree in related field.

**Work Experience:**

Minimum requirements include knowledge and skills developed through 2-5 years of work experience in a related job discipline.

**Certifications:**

------------------

Rippling gives businesses one place to run HR, IT, and Finance. It brings together all of the workforce systems that are normally scattered across a company, like payroll, expenses, benefits, and computers. For the first time ever, you can manage and automate every part of the employee lifecycle in a single system.

Take onboarding, for example. With Rippling, you can hire a new employee anywhere in the world and set up their payroll, corporate card, computer, benefits, and even third-party apps like Slack and Microsoft 365—all within 90 seconds.

Based in San Francisco, CA, Rippling has raised $1.4B+ from the world’s top investors—including Kleiner Perkins, Founders Fund, Sequoia, Greenoaks, and Bedrock—and was named one of America's best startup employers by Forbes.

This is a high-activity, outbound Sales Development role. You’ll be responsible for creating a sales pipeline by researching target accounts, reaching prospects through phone, email, LinkedIn, and other channels, and booking qualified meetings for Account Executives.

It is a focused top-of-funnel role for someone who is energized by prospecting, fast feedback loops, daily activity goals, and a team environment where performance is visible and celebrated. This is not an inbound or full-cycle sales role.

**About Young & Healthy**

Through prevention, education, family support, and access to healthcare services, Young & Healthy protects and improves the physical and mental health of uninsured and underinsured children and their families in the greater Pasadena area. The problem with healthcare services in the Pasadena area is not one of availability, but of affordability and accessibility. One of the greatest obstacles to good health is poverty. In the Pasadena community, about one-third of the children are in need of the kind of care Young & Healthy provides. The majority of children under age 18 and enrolled in Pasadena Unified Schools live in areas of town that claim the lowest per capita income and the greatest concentration of poverty.

Young & Healthy’s model is simple: people helping people. Through collaboration with other community institutions, Young & Healthy makes it a point to know the community and be known by the community so that knowledge and resources can be maximized among community partners to assist the greatest number of neighbors in need.

Young & Healthy is now sustained by the generosity of a volunteer workforce of more than 350 healthcare professionals, over 125 community volunteers and an extensive network of community partners to provide free healthcare to needy underserved children. These professional volunteers agree to see children in their own private offices, on a rotating basis, at no charge to the patient or to Young & Healthy. Young & Healthy facilitates the delivery of donated medical, dental, mental health and other healthcare services, free-of-charge, to underserved low-income children, ranging in age from infancy to 18 years, throughout the greater Pasadena area. In addition to healthcare support, Young & Healthy offers these additional services to the community:

**Health Insurance Assistance** – Young & Healthy helps to prepare families to enroll in and navigate the healthcare system by assisting with health insurance enrollment, providing education and instruction, as well as advocating for clients when they have been wrongfully denied.

**Trauma Informed Care** - Young & Healthy is committed to creating a healthy community for children and families by educating children, parents, and educators on how to become more aware of and sensitive to those who have suffered trauma. new_jobs.description:
**Position:** Inside Sales Representative

**Employment Type:** Regular Full-Time, Non-Exempt

**Schedule:** Monday-Friday, 9 a.m. - 5:30 p.m.

**Department:** Marketing & Communications

**Salary Range:**  $22.00/hour, plus tiered, uncapped commission

**Reports to:** Director of Marketing Analytics & Patron Insights

**About the Role:**

Pacific Symphony is seeking a driven, high-energy Inside Sales Representative to introduce and reintroduce audiences to the world of classical music while generating new institutional revenue. The representative will serve as a primary point of contact for prospective and returning patrons, proactively converting qualified leads into first-time buyers, repeat buyers, Symphony Pass members, and subscribers.

The representative will manage assigned prospects throughout the sales lifecycle, from initial outreach and conversion through follow-up, reengagement, and ongoing cultivation. By developing patron relationships and recommending relevant concerts and ticket products, the representative will help increase repeat attendance, customer lifetime value, and long-term engagement with Pacific Symphony.

This fast-paced, results-oriented role is ideal for individuals who thrive on high-volume outbound outreach, use conversational storytelling to build trust, and love the challenge of closing sales while representing one of Southern California's leading cultural institutions.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* **Lead Conversion:** Conduct high-volume outreach to qualified prospects, converting cold and warm leads into first-time ticket buyers, repeat buyers, Symphony Pass members, and package subscribers.
* **Sales Lifecycle Management:** Manage assigned prospects from initial outreach through conversion, post-purchase follow-up, reengagement, cross-selling, and upgrading. Cultivate buyers toward repeat attendance, multi-ticket purchases, Symphony Pass, and subscription products.
* **Patron Engagement:** Serve as a brand ambassador for Pacific Symphony, using consultative and conversational selling to understand patron interests, recommend relevant concert experiences, address questions, and communicate the value of classical music.
* **Revenue Generation**: Meet and exceed individual sales and revenue targets while developing sustainable pipelines of new and returning patrons.
* **Patron Development:** Build relationships that increase customer lifetime value and encourage deeper engagement with Pacific Symphony. Identify potential philanthropic interest and refer qualified donor opportunities to the Development team for appropriate follow-up.
* **CRM Management:** Maintain accurate and timely records of lead assignments, patron interactions, follow-up activities, opportunity stages, purchases, sales attribution, and pipeline status in the organization’s CRM systems.

**Key Skills & Qualifications:**

· **Experience**: One year experience in inside sales, telemarketing, lead generation, or high-volume call-center environments.

· **Communication**: Exceptional verbal communication, active listening, and rapport-building skills, with a natural ability to use consultative, conversational selling to engage prospects.

· **Resilience**: Goal-oriented, persistent, and able to navigate customer rejection or challenging outbound conversations.

· **Technical Literacy**: Comfortable using standard computer software, CRM platforms, and sales databases.

· **Self-Starter and Team Collaboration**: Highly motivated to meet individual sales goals with minimal supervision while contributing to a collaborative, supportive team environment.

· **Bonus Qualifications**: Familiarity with or enthusiasm for the performing arts, live events, symphonic music, or nonprofit cultural programming.

**Position Focus & Commission Eligibility Rules**

· **Target Audience:** Develop new and returning audiences, with a strategic focus on cultivating patrons with the potential to become repeat buyers, multi-ticket buyers, Symphony Pass members, and subscribers. The role will work from assigned lead lists and campaigns and will not compete with Box Office or existing Telemarketing responsibilities.

· **Eligible Sales:** Commission is earned on eligible single-ticket, Symphony Pass, subscription, reactivation, upgrade, and add-on purchases generated through assigned outreach and properly attributed to the representative.

· **Handoff Policy:** Clear operational workflows are in place for cross-departmental leads. Inbound group sales inquiries, donor upgrades, or structural memberships are handed off to specialized internal departments and do not qualify for base commission.

**Compensation:**

· **Base Compensation + Uncapped Commission:** Receive steady base compensation plus tiered, uncapped commission on eligible and properly attributed net ticket revenue.

· **Tiered Commission Structure:** Commission rates increase as the representative reaches defined annual sales milestones, rewarding new-patron acquisition, returning-patron conversion, and above-target performance.

· **Paid Professional Training:** Thorough, paid onboarding covering Pacific Symphony programming, conversational sales scripting, and database training.

· **Full-Time Benefits Package:** Eligible for Pacific Symphony’s comprehensive benefits, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid holidays, and vacation time.

**Why Join Us:** This is a unique opportunity to build a high-performance sales career while connecting entirely new audiences to world-class live music. As part of our team, you will:

· Gain hands-on experience in inside sales, pipeline management, and live event revenue generation.

· Work within a mission-driven organization that leaves a lasting cultural impact on the Southern California community.

· Learn the inner workings of arts administration alongside a premier cultural institution.

Pay: From $22.00 per hour

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* On-th

**In-Custody Day Program Coordinator**

The Gemma Project is seeking skilled, passionate, and dedicated individuals eager to contribute to our mission of providingand promoting the national creation of gender-responsive jail reentry programming for incarcerated and formerly incarcerated women. The Gemma Project is a trauma responsive, female-led organization that centers integrity and compassion in all the services we provide. Join our team to help us to reduce recidivism, break the intergenerational cycle of incarceration, and create healthier communities.

​​Individuals with a history of justice system involvement are strongly encouraged to apply*.*

**Physical Requirements:**

This position requires approximately 50% of work hours within in-custody jail settings and access to sensitive and protected data and therefore requires but is not limited to completion of Live Scan fingerprinting, and Tuberculosis testing prior to hire and ability *to* abide by all in-custody rules as it relates to attire, personal belongings, materials, conduct, and use of sensitive data.

**How you'll fit in:**

You’ll be a great fit for our team if you are highly skilled, compassionate, and dedicated to providing direct-service reentry programming in an in-custody setting to justice involved women. The Day Program Coordinator works to build rapport and trusting relationships with participants in a group setting prior to release and collaborates with the Continuing Care Coordinator through intentional efforts to maintain participant engagement upon release. The Day Program Coordinator conducts all aspects of running in-custody programming including: interviews, assessments, acceptance decisions; develops, delivers and maintains a relevant, applicable and trauma-responsive curriculum; provides consistent course supervision, safety, and structure to support participants in successful program completion, demonstrates healthy professional boundaries; recruits, trains, and supervises volunteer instructors and works with them to improve and update curricula as needed; works in close collaboration with The Gemma Project Team; supervises and provides direction to the Day Program Assistant; conducts necessary outreach for program; assists in evaluation of program effectiveness; maintains program data and contributes to necessary reports; engages professionally with corrections and community partners as well as funders, donors, and model site visitors.

This position reports to the Executive Director.

**What you'll do:**

* Provide overall operations of Gemma Day Program
* Maintain and update the program curriculum and schedule
* Facilitate core components of curriculum
* Recruit, train and maintain skilled volunteer program instructors
* Support, train, and guide volunteer instructors throughout sessions
* Evaluate instructor performance and make programmatic changes when necessary
* Interview, assess and make admission decisions for all applicants
* Evaluate participant progress and provide feedback to participants as needed
* Provide support and redirection to participants as needed in and out of sessions
* Respond to and document program and participant issues in a clear and timely manner
* Supervise Day Program Assistant(s)
* Coordinate with Continuing Care Coordinator on curriculum and reentry planning to assure seamless support for participants transitioning out of custody
* Collect data to assess program effectiveness and work with Executive Director to make necessary changes based on data
* Maintain accurate and timely records and prepare and submit reports as needed
* Plan and facilitate graduation ceremonies
* Perform outreach/recruitment to encourage program participation
* Perform administrative and clerical duties necessary to the position
* Maintain facility, equipment, and materials
* Attend and actively contribute to team meetings and other organizational meetings
* Attend meetings relevant to community partnerships as needed
* Work in close collaboration with Corrections staff to maintain safety, structure and integrity of program
* Regularly communicate and coordinate with Executive Director and report any concerns
* Support related fund development activities
* Provide health and Medi-Cal outreach, information, referral, eligibility, access assistance, planning and MAA coordination activities
* Perform outreach activities related to Program as needed
* Other duties as assigned

**What you'll bring:**

* Passion for The Gemma Project’s mission and empathy for the unique challenges facing incarcerated and formerly incarcerated women
* Commitment to positively contributing to a diverse, equitable, inclusive, and trauma responsive organizational culture through self-awareness, cultural humility, and valuing others
* Dedication to supporting and celebrating female identified individuals in their healing, development, and contributions to the community
* A reputation for a high standard of honesty, integrity, and professionalism
* A curious, detail-oriented, and problem-solving mindset focused on centering gender and trauma responsive services
* The ability to create and maintain collaborative relationships across other functional areas to solve problems, and improve programs, systems, and outcomes for participants
* Receptivity to feedback and ability to ask for and accept help
* The ability to find joy in our work, contribute to optimism, and celebrate individual and team achievements
* Exceptional skill at creating and maintaining a safe, structured, supportive, and trauma-responsive learning environment for participants
* Strong group facilitation and management skills including the ability to maximize participation and engage individuals with different learning styles and abilities
* Strong oral communication skills, including the ability to diffuse and deescalate challenging situations, distill and present complex information in a concise, accessible way, and capability of delivering difficult info

**Location:** San Francisco, CA; 5 days in office/week

**Status:** Full time; non-exempt (40 hours/week FT NE)

**Salary:** $62,000 - $67,000/year

**Reports to:** Program Director

**Organization Description**

The Miss Major Alexander L. Lee TGIJP Black Trans Cultural Center is a team of transgender, gender-variant and intersex people, inside and outside of prisons, jails, detention centers, and other locked facilities creating a united family in the struggle for survival and freedom. We work in collaboration with others to forge a culture of resistance and resilience to strengthen us for the fight against human rights abuses, imprisonment, police violence, racism, poverty, and societal pressures. We seek to create a world rooted in self-determination, freedom of expression, and gender justice.

**Position Description**

TGIJP’s Client Services Coordinators are the first to greet our clients, staff, partners, Board Members, and other community members when they come into our office. First impressions are everything when it comes to telegraphing safety, security, empowerment, trauma-informed care, and an abolitionist mindset to all we meet. You’re expected to know how to work with dozens of different kinds of people effectively, to know how to appropriately prioritize and execute administrative and operational tasks, and to be able to maintain a level of professionalism, pleasant demeanor, and grounded approach to the work.

new_jobs.description:
**Center for Latino Adolescent and Family Health at Johns Hopkins School of Nursing**

**Title of Position:** LPN Clinical Research Coordinator

The Center for Latino Adolescent and Family Health’s (CLAFH’s) mission is to eliminate health inequities and promote overall wellbeing among Latino adolescents and their families. While our work is Latino-focused, our research and resources are applicable to initiatives aimed at ending inequities for other groups. CLAFH’s core work focuses on developing, evaluating, and disseminating family-based interventions and nurse-driven models of health care delivery designed to mitigate harmful social determinants of health, eliminate health inequities, increase Latino engagement in health care, and promote life opportunities. For more information about our center, please see our website.

**Description of Duties and Responsibilities**

The **LPN** Clinical Research Coordinator will oversee the day-to-day implementation of CLAFH's community-based behavioral health and prevention programs, with a focus on coordinating field operations, supervising research and program staff, and supporting the delivery of nurse-led and family-centered services. The position will involve direct engagement with adolescents, young adults, and families, primarily in the South Bronx.

The LPN Clinical Research Coordinator will:

* Oversee daily field operations and implementation of community-based health and prevention programs, including home visits, community outreach, screening, prevention education, and referral and linkage to services.
* Coordinate and supervise field-based research and program staff, including community health workers, family coaches, and other personnel involved in program implementation.
* Develop and coordinate staff schedules, field assignments, training activities, and ongoing supervision to ensure timely and effective program delivery.
* Perform clinical duties within the scope of LPN licensure, including health screenings, patient education, documentation, and other nursing services under appropriate clinical supervision.
* Oversee participant recruitment, enrollment, retention, follow-up, and fidelity to evidence-based and community-derived intervention protocols.
* Support nurse-led care coordination, including identifying participant health and social needs, facilitating referrals, and following up with families to support engagement in appropriate services.
* Coordinate with community partners, health care providers, and social service organizations to support program implementation and strengthen referral and linkage processes.
* Monitor program activities, service delivery, and staff performance to ensure adherence to project protocols, quality standards, and funder requirements.
* Work collaboratively with project leadership and evaluation staff to ensure accurate and timely collection, documentation, and reporting of participant and program data.
* Assist with continuous quality improvement activities, identifying implementation challenges and opportunities to strengthen program reach, engagement, and service delivery.
* Ensure adherence to relevant confidentiality, participant protection, ethical, and regulatory requirements, including HIPAA and applicable human subjects research protocols.
* Support preparation for project meetings, staff trainings, site visits, and other program-related activities.
* Perform other duties as assigned in support of CLAFH's community-based research and intervention programs.

**Qualifications for the Position**

* Current, unrestricted Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN) license in New York State required.
* Graduate of an accredited practical nursing program required.
* Experience in community health, public health, adolescent health, behavioral health, or related service delivery settings preferred.
* Experience coordinating or supervising community-based research or program staff preferred.
* Experience implementing evidence-based interventions, conducting health screenings, and supporting care coordination preferred.
* Familiarity with substance use prevention, mental health services, and health and social service systems preferred.
* Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish preferred.
* Bronx residency and familiarity with South Bronx communities preferred.
* Experience working with Latino, Black, and other historically underserved communities preferred.
* Strong organizational, interpersonal, supervisory, and communication skills.
* Ability to manage multiple program activities and coordinate staff in a fast-paced, deadline-focused environment.
* Willingness and ability to work in community-based settings, including participant homes and partner organizations.
* Flexibility to work occasional evenings or weekends as needed for community outreach and program activities.
* Strong commitment to addressing health inequities and supporting adolescent and family wellbeing.

**Supervisory Relationships:** Reports to the Principal Investigator and designated CLAFH leadership. Provides operational supervision to assigned field-based research and program staff. Clinical duties are performed under the supervision required by applicable New York State nursing regulations.

Pay: $60,000.00 - $70,000.00 per year

Work Location: In person

new_jobs.description:
**Department**

BSD IPP - MOSAAIC

**About the Department**

The Institute for Population and Precision Health (IPPH), located in the Biological Sciences Division, integrates a wide spectrum of factors such as human health behaviors, environmental factors, social and economic factors, policies and genetic determinants of health, into studies focused on the treatment and prevention of disease, as well as the maintenance of wellness. Leveraging and integrating the University of Chicago’s considerable institutional strength in population science with research spanning diverse fields such as genetic medicine, cancer epidemiology, microbiome, and epigenomics, the Institute will have the common goal of improving human health outcomes. Another major goal of the Institute will be to develop a new multidisciplinary training program to equip researchers with emerging tools and methods to conduct precision health research within a population health framework. Our faculty lead research projects in biostatistics, epidemiology and health services research and participate in interdisciplinary teams with faculty in other departments to address complex problems in health and healthcare, in our communities and around the globe.

**Job Summary**

The University of Chicago's Institute for Population and Precision Health (IPPH) is seeking a Clinical Research Coordinator 2 to support its portfolio of federally funded population health research, with a primary focus on the Multi-ethnic Observational Study in American Asian and Pacific Islander Communities (MOSAAIC) — a landmark NHLBI-funded epidemiological cohort study aimed at addressing critical gaps in cardiovascular, metabolic, pulmonary, and mental health research for Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander communities.  
  
The University of Chicago serves as one of five national clinical and community field centers for MOSAAIC, with a goal of enrolling 2,000 Chicago-area participants through community-based outreach, mobile data collection, clinical phenotyping, and biospecimen collection. The study collects data across a broad range of health domains, including heart health, diabetes, lung health, and mental health, as well as social determinants of health such as environmental exposures and access to care. The Clinical Research Coordinator 2 will support the full research lifecycle across this and related IPPH studies — including participant recruitment and retention, IRB compliance, data and specimen collection, quality control, and milestone reporting — working closely with Scientific Directors and the Research Manager to advance research that promotes health equity and reduces disparities in historically underrepresented populations.  
  
This at-will position is wholly or partially funded by contractual grant funding which is renewed under provisions set by the grantor of the contract. Employment will be contingent upon the continued receipt of these grant funds and satisfactory job performance.

**Responsibilities**

* Coordination and quality control management for observational and interventional, including both clinic and community-based studies, within the Institute for Population and Precision Health.
* Support operational execution of multi-institutional and some international studies, many of which are federally funded or funded by pharmaceutical sponsors.
* Oversee the collection of clinical data, survey data, environmental data, and associated samples and biospecimens.
* Manage IRB submissions, amendments, and continuing reviews; develop and refine data collection instruments; enforce implementation accuracy and study staff protocol compliance; and deliver continuous milestone reporting — including progress, successes, and emerging challenges — to study leadership.

* Monitor study participants, schedule, and conduct study-related procedures (eg. interviews, phlebotomies, and follow-ups) and establish data quality control checks.

* Assist in the development of new projects and preparation of study reports, and manuscripts for publication.
* Assist in the preparation of presentations, media, and curricular materials relating to research.
* Accountable for all tasks in moderately complex clinical studies.
* Assists with various professional, organizational, and operational tasks under moderate supervision.
* Facilitates and participates in the daily activities of moderately complex clinical studies and performs various activities including patient data retrieval, documenting clinical research records, and participation in program audits.
* Uses knowledge of clinical studies to coordinate the collection of analyzable clinical research data and/or samples with a limited to moderate degree of independence. Contributes to the problem solving on assigned clinical research studies and tasks.
* Performs other related work as needed.

**Education:**

Minimum requirements include a college or university degree in related field.

**Work Experience:**

**Certifications:**

**-**

**Education:**

Collaboration is key—we thrive on teamwork, open communication, and diverse perspectives. In a field that constantly changes, we value those who are resilient, adaptable, and resourceful in the face of challenges. If you're intellectually curious, eager to learn, and ready to help restore ecosystems and protect natural resources, you'll find your place here.

**RES** is seeking a **Client Solutions Manager** that will market integrated delivery projects directly to prospects and clients in mitigation, water quality, and resilience. The position is vital to the region's sales and business development function and promotes RES solutions throughout the Southeast region, including North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, and Georgia. * You'll be on the front lines of delivering real environmental results—through deals that matter.

You'll work closely with land, regulatory, design, and project teams to pursue and win business opportunities in your assigned market. From guiding internal teams on project pursuit strategy to presenting financial summaries to clients, you'll be the connector between RES capabilities and market opportunities—bringing deals from idea to execution.

**About Rippling**
------------------

Rippling gives businesses one place to run HR, IT, and Finance. It brings together all of the workforce systems that are normally scattered across a company, like payroll, expenses, benefits, and computers. For the first time ever, you can manage and automate every part of the employee lifecycle in a single system.

Take onboarding, for example. With Rippling, you can hire a new employee anywhere in the world and set up their payroll, corporate card, computer, benefits, and even third-party apps like Slack and Microsoft 365—all within 90 seconds.

Based in San Francisco, CA, Rippling has raised $1.4B+ from the world’s top investors—including Kleiner Perkins, Founders Fund, Sequoia, Greenoaks, and Bedrock—and was named one of America's best startup employers by Forbes.

We prioritize candidate safety. Please be aware that all official communication will only be sent from @Rippling.com addresses.

**About the role**
------------------

This is a high-activity, outbound Sales Development role. You’ll be responsible for creating a sales pipeline by researching target accounts, reaching prospects through phone, email, LinkedIn, and other channels, and booking qualified meetings for Account Executives.

It is a focused top-of-funnel role for someone who is energized by prospecting, fast feedback loops, daily activity goals, and a team environment where performance is visible and celebrated. This is not an inbound or full-cycle sales role.

You’ll learn Rippling’s full platform, understand the operational pain points our customers face, and build the foundation for a long-term career in sales. Successful SDRs typically spend time in-seat developing core prospecting, discovery, objection-handling, and territory-management skills before furthering their sales career.  
  
***(This is a hybrid role and you will be required to be in the office 3x per week in Chicago, IL)***

**What you'll do**
------------------

* Research target companies, personas, business triggers, and operational pain points to identify high-quality prospecting opportunities
* Prospect into target accounts using phone, email, LinkedIn, and sales engagement tools
* Own a high-volume outbound motion, including daily call blocks, email follow-ups, account research, and multi-touch sequences
* Work toward clear daily and weekly activity expectations, including roughly 80–100 calls and 40–50 emails per day, depending on territory priorities and team guidance
* Qualify prospects using defined criteria and schedule high-quality meetings for Account Executives
* Partner closely with Account Executives on territory strategy, account prioritization, messaging, and follow-ups
* Participate actively in weekly enablement sessions, team call reviews, and manager coaching; apply feedback quickly to improve your messaging, objection handling, and overall prospecting effectiveness
* Maintain accurate records in Salesforce and keep outreach, account, and prospect data clean
* Leverage tools like Salesforce, Outreach, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, ZoomInfo, Apollo, and dialer technology to execute efficiently

**Qualifications**

* BA/BS degree or equivalent work experience
* A high sense of urgency and genuine interest in a sales career
* Strong communication skills, especially over the phone and in concise, written outreach
* Coachability - you can take feedback, apply it quickly, and improve from one call to the next
* Curiosity and initiative - you ask good questions, seek context, and look for ways to get better without waiting to be told
* Resilience and consistency in a high-activity prospecting environment

* Ability to collaborate cross-functionally with sales, marketing, and other teams

**What success looks like**

In your first 30 days, you’ll focus on onboarding, product knowledge, sales methodology, tools, messaging, and understanding Rippling’s customers.

By month two, you’ll begin ramping into live prospecting, building activity consistency, and working toward partial quota expectations.

By month three, you should be operating at full ramp expectations, managing daily outbound activity, booking qualified meetings, and showing consistent improvement through coaching and repetition.
